basis: Adopted 2026-10-29 02:40 from docs/proposals/shape-rules-v2.md after the first tuning-loop session (plan item 8). Four rules: saturated (unchanged from shape_v1) and three added by the loop: shadow_strong (bright candidates with a strong one-sided shadow of a height in 0.5 to 3 m), dark_shadow (dark compact candidates with their own shadow of that height) and tile_top (the strongest bright component in its 2048 px tile). Each gain is minus log10 of the rule's measured pass fraction among the bright, shadow or dark_compact false alarms of the eight tuning strips (out/shape_v1/candidates_v02b_features.json). Measured together: key recall@20 8 of 18 (hardware 7 of 12) against 6 of 18 for shape_v1; transplant injection hardware 35 of 72 against 31, fabric 9 of 24 against 10. tile_top is a test of the neighbourhood rather than the object and is kept on the condition that the leave-one-site-out check in plan item 8 confirms its lift on sites it was not fitted on; if not, it is withdrawn before the frozen tag and the other three stay. Re-measure and re-version whenever the detector changes.

rules.name: saturated
rules.basis: landers/shape_v1.json: at least one pixel at the sensor's saturation; natural ground at HiRISE exposure rarely saturates, bright hardware often does

rules.name: shadow_strong
rules.basis: dark on the anti-sun side only, far beyond what polygon troughs and slopes produce, with a length that reads as a 0.5 to 3 m object; bright branch only, the shadow branch already selects on this

rules.name: dark_shadow
rules.basis: a dark object that still casts a shadow of the right length stands above the ground; a dark patch in the ground does not

rules.name: tile_top
rules.basis: the brightest compact object within its 2048 px detector tile; a test of the surroundings rather than the object, see the proposal's caveats
